findings.problem: The guard never checks that a page actually begins inside an optional clause in this unit. It only checks four things: no open condition scope, continuation on current_page with page_start False, every earlier on-page fragment in the unit has page_start False, and no earlier deferral on that page. Existing data commonly sets page_start False on every fragment of a unit that starts mid-page, because the page's pb belongs to an earlier unit's file (the Kedushah fixture is like this for all of s9). So a unit that starts mid-page, has a conditional segment, and then a deferred_page_boundary segment passes every check. It emits a second pb for a page that began in another file, which is exactly the duplicate the feature says it rejects. The guard also accepts unconditional segments with explicit page_start False between the clause and the deferred segment, so 'first unconditional continuation' is not enforced. pb@n comes from the continuation's printed_page and is never compared with the transition fragment's printed_page. The test has no 'wrong page' case (continuation on another scan) and no mid-page-unit case. Its three negatives cover only the page_start True duplicate, a conditioned continuation, and a repeated deferral.
findings.required_fix: Find the first fragment on current_page in this unit. Require that (a) an earlier fragment in the same unit is on a different scan, so there is a real transition inside the unit; (b) that fragment belongs to a conditional segment, or lies inside a condition_end_corresp scope that closes immediately before this segment; (c) every segment from the transition up to this one is inside that conditional scope, so this is the first unconditional segment after it; and (d) the continuation's printed_page equals the transition fragment's printed_page. Add negative tests for a unit starting mid-page (all page_start False, conditional, then deferred), an intervening unconditional page_start False segment, a continuation on a different scan ('wrong page'), a mismatched printed_page, and deferred_page_boundary set to a non-True value.

findings.problem: deferred_page_boundary deliberately moves a facsimile boundary away from its scan position, but it is not in the literal review payload. Adding or removing it on a new unit does not make that unit's review stale. On an accepted unit the baseline protected hash would catch it, but on new batch units only review would.
findings.required_fix: When the flag is set, append a fixed marker such as '[page boundary deferred after optional clause]' to unit_review_text. This leaves every existing hash unchanged. Add a test that toggling the flag changes the review text.

findings.problem: The build gate does not trigger on segment 'canonical'/'canonical_end' or on a canonical_home without context_urn. A redirect inside an existing unit with no page_context therefore relies only on the CI unit test. The build uses the source-tree baseline named by readings.json, while CI uses the importer fixture, and nothing checks that the two copies match. No build-level test exercises the gate (missing baseline raises; a path outside the source book raises).
findings.required_fix: Widen the gate to any canonical_home, segment canonical or canonical_whole, or else document why the CI test is enough. Once the data commit adds accepted_literal_baseline, add a test that readings.json names it and that its content equals the fixture. Add two build tests in the tempfile harness: canonical_parts with no baseline must raise, and a baseline path outside the source must raise.
